If it's no big deal, then why have contesting rules at all?

ACTUALLY, using both Camille and Raven isn't really that different
than pasting a new name on another vampire and claiming that it's now
unique. I find that one of the biggest problems I have when designing decks
is finding enough suitable vampires. Of the three decks I have, one of them
duplicates 2 vamps and triplicates 1 and another deck duplicates 3 and
triplicates 2. I don't do this because I love these specific vampires
(although it's hard not to love Ozmo), but because my decks have VERY
specific themes and it's hard to find vampires that fit the requirements
for the deck. Belive me, I would love to have three identical Biancas with
different names so I can claim that they are each unique, but the game
has unique vampires for a reason (at least I hope the ruls have some
reason behind them. Don't they Tom?) and considering Raven and Cammile
different vampires because the company is attempting to avoid a law suit
just seems to be a stupid way to get around game restrictions. I'm not
saying that this has a huge impact on the game, but I am saying that it
is detrimental to game balance in it's own small way.

Also, someone said that they thought that the Gangrel had been
shafted diversity-wize. To this I say, "Look at the Toreador sometime!"
The Toreador are simply the least diverse clan, with access to fewer
different disciplines than any other clan in the game. They also don't
have the benefit of access to such diverse disciplines as animalism and
protean. All in all, I'd give the advantage to the Gangrel.

Same principle, different stats. Having vampires of same capacity and same
disciplines just isn't that big of a deal. And if it is a real benefit, it's
a self-limiting benefit, just as with any unique card: if the cards are that
good, it's that much more likely that you'll be contesting the cards, or not
playing them in the first place to avoid contention.

If a 2-capacity vampire is going to be useful for your deck, then having two
of them will be more useful. If a 5-capacity vampire is going to be useful
for your deck, then having two of them will be more useful. The only
difference is that the 5-capacity vampire is going to fit into more deck
concepts, but again, this is a self-limiting advantage.

The tournament rules state:

player's cards will only be allowed if all players at the table agree to
allow them in the round. If any player(s) at the table do not wish card
sleeves to be used in the round for any reason, all sleeves must be
removed from all decks at that table for the duration of the
round.

split, but I do have opaque or double packed sleeves. If ONE player at

illegal mix, so he asks me to remove my sleeves, oh look at that I lose.
